terms.grammar: adjective (participle of contineō), with the ablative
evidence: Cic. Sen. 69: eō dēbet esse contentus
terms.comment: From contineō, hold together, hold in: one who keeps within bounds, and so is satisfied with what he has. The same form is also the participle of contendō, stretch, strain: contentus, taut, intent (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: learn to be content with little

phrases.latin: quod cuique temporis ad vīvendum datur, eō dēbet esse contentus
phrases.english: whatever time each of us is given to live, with that he ought to be content

phrases.latin: nēmō nāscitur dīves; quisquis exit in lūcem jussus est lacte et pannō esse contentus
phrases.english: no one is born rich: whoever comes into the light is told to be content with milk and a rag
and all are content with their own gifts

sources: Lewis & Short: contentus · Lewis & Short: contineo
